title: Label epistemic status in public
principle: Maggie Appleton’s digital-garden ethos: publish imperfect work, but make incompleteness legible. Seedling / budding / evergreen (or draft / certainty / effort tags à la Gwern and Devon Zuegel) tell readers how done a note is. For AI craft desks, status labels stop agents and humans from treating a half-formed prompt pack like canon.
procedure: Pick a small status vocabulary (e.g. seedling / budding / evergreen) and define each in one line.
Put status + planted/last-tended dates on every public craft note, technique draft, or prompt pack.
Optionally add certainty or effort tags when claims could be over-read as settled truth.
Update status when you tend the note—growth is visible, not hidden behind a silent edit.
Teach agents: never upgrade a seedling to evergreen without human or critic review.
examplePrompts:
Add garden status labels (Maggie Appleton ethos) to these docs:
- Vocabulary: seedling (rough), budding (clarified), evergreen (reasonably complete, still tendable).
- Each page gets status + planted date + last-tended date in the header.
- Do not rewrite seedling content to sound finished—label honesty beats fake polish.
Return the header pattern and apply it.
Audit this technique page: if worked examples are thin or sources are partial, set status to budding and add a one-line coverage note. Never imply paywalled depth you do not have.
promptWhy: Forces honesty about completeness—the failure mode of AI catalogs is sounding finished when thin.
Ties status to source coverage so Deliver-stage pages cannot bluff past paywalls.
tips: Gardens favour topography over timelines—status matters more than publish date.
Learning in public only works if imperfection is disclosed (Appleton’s pattern 3).
Pair with sources.json coverage notes already used in this catalog.
Keep Quiet Folio paper/ink if applying on this desk—no purple chrome.

workedExamples.title: Seedling vs evergreen technique
workedExamples.before: Thin TC-EBC stub presented with the same chrome as a full Anshu technique—readers assume equal depth.
workedExamples.after: Budding label + coverage note (‘public Figma blog paraphrase; no course reprint’) sets expectations.
workedExamples.body: Appleton: gardens make imperfection known. This catalog’s sources already use coverage fields; status labels extend that to the page chrome.

workedExamples.title: Planted / last tended
workedExamples.body: Maggie’s own essays show planted and last-tended timestamps so readers see growth. Agents should bump last-tended when they deepen a technique.

workedExamples.title: Terms of service for gardens
workedExamples.body: Shawn Wang’s digital gardening TOS (cited in Appleton’s essay) asks writers for epistemic disclosure and readers for constructive critique—useful norms for public craft desks.

antiPatterns: Shipping unfinished prompt packs with authoritative tone and no status.
Using status as decoration without definitions.
Silently editing evergreen pages into contradiction without a tend note.
checklist: Status vocabulary defined on the desk.
Public craft pages show status + dates.
Agents forbidden from silent evergreen upgrades.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Stop when the named task is clearer and acceptance evidence is recorded; do not add polish without a problem.
